topics.title: Graphs
topics.outcome: Read a graph from a picture and from Python
topics.goal: Read a graph from a picture and from Python, using the right words. Covers objectives 1 and 2.

sections.title: What a graph is
text: A **graph** is a set of **vertices** (dots) joined by **edges** (lines). It only records *which* things are connected, not where they are or how far apart.
A road map, a group of friends and the links between web pages are all graphs.

chapters.label: A map
chapters.caption: A map with six buildings and the paths between them.

chapters.label: Buildings become vertices
chapters.caption: Swap each building for a vertex.

chapters.label: Paths become edges
chapters.caption: Swap each path for an edge.

chapters.label: Only connections
chapters.caption: Distances and positions don't matter. Only who is connected.

chapters.label: Neighbours
chapters.caption: C's neighbours are A, D and E. Its degree is 3.

chapters.label: Isolated
chapters.caption: F has no edges. It's an isolated vertex.

sections.q: How many vertices and how many edges does our graph have?
sections.a: 6 vertices (A to F) and 5 edges (A–B, A–C, B–D, C–D, C–E).

sections.title: Words you need
text: These words come up in every graph question, in this course and in the lecture.

rows: One dot. Also called a node
A, B, C, D, E, F
C's neighbours are A, D and E
How many edges touch a vertex
C has degree 3; E has degree 1
A route along edges, with no vertex repeated
The number of edges on the path (not vertices)
Every vertex can reach every other
Not our graph, because of F

sections.q: What is the degree of D, and who are its neighbours?
sections.a: Degree 2. Its neighbours are B and C.

sections.title: Edges go both ways and cost the same
text: Our edges are **undirected**: the edge A–B lets you go from A to B *and* from B to A, so B is in A's list and A is in B's list.
They are also **unweighted**: every edge counts as one step, so "shortest" means *fewest edges*.

Two other kinds exist. They're shown here once for contrast and not used again. **Directed** edges are one-way arrows, like a one-way street. **Weighted** edges carry a number, like a distance in km; shortest then means the smallest total, which needs a different algorithm (Dijkstra's), not BFS.

sections.q: The edge C–E is undirected. Which two neighbour lists contain it?
sections.a: C's list has E, and E's list has C.

sections.title: Storing a graph in Python
text: We store the graph as an **adjacency list**: a dictionary where each vertex maps to the list of its neighbours.
An adjacency list only stores the edges that exist, so it stays small. The other common way is a grid of 0s and 1s with one row and one column per vertex (an **adjacency matrix**).
Press Run to see what the code prints, or try one of the tasks.

tasks.q: Predict, then run: what does graph["F"] print?
tasks.why: F has no neighbours: it's an isolated vertex.

tasks.q: Predict, then run: is A in D's list?
tasks.why: D's neighbours are B and C. A is two edges away from D.

tasks.q: Predict, then run: how many edges does the graph have?
tasks.why: Each undirected edge is stored twice (once in each list), so the list lengths add up to 10.

sections.q: What does graph["F"] print, and what does that tell you?
sections.a: [] — F has no neighbours, so it's an isolated vertex.

sections.title: Practice exercises
text: Longer questions. Try each one on paper first.

items.q: Write the adjacency list for the edges P–Q, P–R, Q–S.
A student writes "A": ["B"] but forgets to put A in B's list. What goes wrong?
items.a: The graph now says you can go from A to B but not back. That makes it directed, which is wrong for an undirected edge.

items.q: Which vertex in our graph has the highest degree?
Is A → B → D → C a path, and how long is it?
items.a: Yes. It has 3 edges, so its length is 3.

items.q: Name a real thing you'd model with directed edges, and one with weighted edges.
items.a: Any sensible answer, e.g. social-media follows (directed) and road distances (weighted).

sections.title: Module 2 quiz
text: 5 questions. Answer them all, then press Submit.

questions.no: An edge is one line between two vertices.
B's list is [A, D]: one edge to each.
F has no edges at all. E has one edge (to C).

questions.q: In an unweighted graph, what does "shortest route" mean?
questions.no: Every edge counts as one step, so shortest = fewest edges.

topics.recap: A graph is vertices joined by edges. Ours are undirected and unweighted, and Python stores them as an adjacency list.
